title: A Two-Level System Cannot Achieve a Population Inversion
lead: A laser's light must come from stimulated emission, which has to outrun absorption in the medium. The medium here is an idealized atom with only two energy levels, driven by a pump.
notes: Adapted from Newman, Maleki and Neils, shared under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
exercise_notes: The section prints no exercises; the one here is new and AI-written, its answer checked by computation, and its Bloom level and concept tags were chosen by AI.

figures.original_caption: A two-level lasing system. (CC BY-NC; Ümit Kaya via LibreTexts)

exercises.source_id: Achieving population inversion in a two-level atom is not very practical.
exercises.prompt: A pump drives the two levels of an atom with $g_1 = g_2$. Its light gives $B_{12}\rho_{\nu}(\nu_{12}) = 4.0 \times 10^{6}\ \text{s}^{-1}$, and the upper level decays spontaneously with $A_{21} = 1.0 \times 10^{6}\ \text{s}^{-1}$. Find the steady-state ratio $N_2/N_1$ (a) for this pump and (b) for a pump ten times as strong.

parts.hint: Set dN₂/dt in (15.2.2) to zero with B₂₁ = B₁₂ and solve for N₂/N₁.

answer.solution: At steady state (15.2.2) gives $0 = B_{12} ho_{ u}N_1 - A_{21}N_2 - B_{21} ho_{ u}N_2$, and with $B_{21} = B_{12}$ this is $N_2/N_1 = B_{12} ho_{ u}/(A_{21} + B_{12} ho_{ u})$. (a) $4.0/(1.0 + 4.0) = 0.80$. (b) $40/(1.0 + 40) = 0.976$. Ten times the pump moves the ratio closer to 1, but $A_{21}$ in the denominator keeps it below 1 for any pump, so the two levels never invert.

footnotes.html: (15.2.11) gives $g_1B_{12} = g_2B_{21}$, so $B_{21} = B_{12}$ holds when the two levels have the same degeneracy, $g_1 = g_2$, as the two-level atom here is taken to have.

Steady pumping cannot do it at any cost. At steady state the rate equation (15.2.2) gives $N_2/N_1 = B_{12}\rho_{\nu}/(A_{21} + B_{12}\rho_{\nu})$, which stays below 1 however strong the pump, as the opening of 15.4 says: optical pumping at most equalizes the two populations.

derivations.source: Physical Chemistry (LibreTexts), 15.3 A Two-Level System Cannot Achieve a Population Inversion

assumes.text: Under a steady pump the populations stop changing, $dN_2(t)/dt = 0$.

steps.cap: The denominator exceeds the numerator by $A_{21}$, which is positive, so the ratio stays below 1 and reaches it only as $\krhonu$ grows without limit.
